stem: According to the provided material, how is conjugated jaundice defined biochemically?

options.text: Conjugated fraction $\ge 20\%$ of the total bilirubin
Conjugated fraction $\ge 50\%$ of the total bilirubin
Total bilirubin above the $95^{th}$ centile for age
The presence of any detectable conjugated bilirubin in the serum

explanation: This specific threshold distinguishes conjugated hyperbilirubinemia from other forms of neonatal jaundice.
rationale: Focus on the ratio of the conjugated portion relative to the total bilirubin level.

optionExplanations.A: This specific threshold distinguishes conjugated hyperbilirubinemia from other forms of neonatal jaundice.
optionExplanations.B: While a value this high is certainly abnormal, the clinical threshold for investigation begins at a lower percentage.
optionExplanations.C: Total bilirubin levels determine the presence of jaundice but not the specific subtype (conjugated vs. unconjugated) required for diagnosis.
optionExplanations.D: Small amounts of conjugated bilirubin may be present normally; a specific percentage of the total is required for a pathological definition.

source.hint: Focus on the ratio of the conjugated portion relative to the total bilirubin level.
